promise: Bring one task you keep doing. Leave with one assistant you can use again.
practice_notice: Andrew provides this ready-made practice example during the lab. Teachers do not need to prepare lesson materials or use real student information to learn the method.

scenario.title: Riverton Public Space Choice
scenario.label: Practice copy: no real people or records
scenario.week_question: How should a public space reflect a community's priorities?
scenario.week_objective: Compare two practice proposals, evaluate each against stated criteria, and support a recommendation with evidence.

proposal_a.name: Library Link Plaza
facts: Small performance platform and water fountain
Wide path connecting the library to the bus stop

proposal_b.name: Market Garden Commons
facts: 36 raised garden beds and a shade pavilion
Outdoor classroom and weekend produce stand
Standard pedestrian entrance with no direct bus-stop connection

rough_notes.notes: Opening question: What makes a public space welcoming? Introduce the three criteria. Preview both proposal summaries. Exit response: Which criterion matters most and why?
Pairs read both proposal summaries. Complete comparison chart. Circle one strong piece of evidence for each proposal.
Model an evidence-based recommendation. Small groups draft one recommendation and cite two facts. Brief share-out.
Peer feedback and revision. I have not chosen the time breakdown or whether feedback will be on paper or digital.
Gallery walk: 20 minutes. Individual reflection: 15 minutes. Need a closing move for the remaining time.

assistant_setup.label: Help me with
assistant_setup.text: Turn my rough weekly lesson notes into my weekly lesson format.

assistant_setup.label: Use only
assistant_setup.text: The blank format, rough notes, and practice proposal summaries I provide for this task.

assistant_setup.label: Return
assistant_setup.text: For each day, return the objective, materials, sequence and timing, student directions, two teacher check questions, and decisions still needed.

assistant_setup.label: Stop and ask if
assistant_setup.text: Timing, materials, or a required fact is missing. Use only the text or files I give you for this task. If the information is not there, mark NEEDS TEACHER INPUT instead of guessing.

assistant_setup.label: I will review
assistant_setup.text: Accuracy, appropriateness, alignment, missing information, accessibility, and final wording.

exact_request: Use my saved Weekly Lesson Setup Assistant instructions. Complete the blank weekly format from the rough notes and the two practice proposal summaries. Keep every claim tied to the material I provided. Mark missing decisions as NEEDS TEACHER INPUT.

first_result.objective: Identify the three criteria used to compare the two proposals.
first_result.materials: Proposal summaries; criteria chart; exit slip
first_result.sequence: Opening question 6 min; criteria mini-lesson 12 min; proposal preview 20 min; exit response 10 min
first_result.directions: Name one feature that could make a public space welcoming. Then use the three criteria to notice differences between the proposals.
first_result.checks: Can students name all three criteria? Can they connect a feature to one criterion?

first_result.objective: Compare the two proposals and select evidence for each.
first_result.sequence: Directions 5 min; partner reading 18 min; chart 17 min; evidence check 8 min
first_result.directions: Read both summaries. Record one strength and one tradeoff for each. Both proposals include a direct connection to the bus stop.
first_result.checks: Did each claim come from a proposal summary? Did students record evidence for both proposals?

first_result.objective: Draft a recommendation supported by two facts.
first_result.materials: Model paragraph; proposal summaries; draft sheet
first_result.sequence: Model 10 min; group drafting 23 min; share-out 15 min
first_result.directions: Choose one proposal. State your recommendation and support it with two facts from the summaries.
first_result.checks: Is the recommendation clear? Are both facts accurate and relevant?

first_result.objective: Use peer feedback to strengthen a recommendation.
first_result.directions: Give one note about evidence and one note about clarity. Revise after reviewing the feedback.
first_result.checks: Is the feedback specific? Does the revision improve evidence or clarity?
first_result.decisions: NEEDS TEACHER INPUT: paper or digital feedback

first_result.objective: Explain and reflect on a final recommendation.
first_result.materials: Final recommendation; gallery response sheet; reflection prompt
first_result.sequence: Gallery walk 20 min; reflection 15 min; NEEDS TEACHER INPUT: closing move for remaining 13 min
first_result.directions: Read several recommendations. Notice how evidence shaped each choice. Complete the reflection.
first_result.checks: Did the reflection use evidence? Can students explain one tradeoff?

review.visible_mistake: The Tuesday draft says both proposals connect directly to the bus stop. Only Library Link Plaza does.
review.missing_information: The assistant correctly marked Thursday timing, Thursday format, and Friday closing as teacher decisions instead of inventing them.
teacher_choices: Set Thursday timing to 6 minutes directions, 12 minutes partner feedback, 22 minutes revision, and 8 minutes closing check.
Use Friday's remaining 13 minutes for a 5-minute partner debrief, a 5-minute whole-group synthesis, and a 3-minute exit check.
Display directions and read them aloud before independent work.

final_result_changes: Tuesday now states that only Library Link Plaza has a direct bus-stop connection.
Thursday includes a complete 48-minute sequence and names paper feedback.
Friday includes a complete closing sequence for the remaining 13 minutes.
Directions are displayed and read aloud before independent work.
The teacher review line remains visible: The assistant prepares. The teacher decides.

reuse.next_week: Replace only the rough notes and task materials. Keep the five-part setup, then review the new result before use.
reuse.measure: For two weeks, compare the usual planning time with assistant time plus correction and review time. Keep, revise, or stop based on actual usefulness.
